title: improv·artist · spiritual (Hilma af Klint)
mutation_directive: improv artist: spiritual via Hilma af Klint

improv_extras.practice: esoteric geometry; spirals, mandalas, color-coded cosmology; visions made diagrammatic

v1.feedback: The Hilma af Klint brief asks for esoteric geometry — spirals, mandalas, color-coded cosmology — but the piece is fundamentally a Lucy point-cloud that occasionally morphs into a flat concentric-ring mandala. The mandala geometry is too simple (evenly spaced rings with minimal dome curvature) and reads more like a disc than a sacred diagram; it needs layered nested circles, petal overlaps, or triangulated subdivisions that reference Klint's actual paintings. The palette (gold/rose/blue/cream) is the strongest nod to the brief and is genuinely restrained, but the Lucy statue half of the cycle has nothing to do with Hilma af Klint and feels like leftover scaffold from a different piece — drop Lucy entirely and invest those 60k particles in a richer mandala with concentric symbol bands, spiraling petals, and a slow radial bloom that evokes diagrammatic vision rather than a 3D-scan showcase.

v2.feedback: The mandala structure clearly channels Hilma af Klint's concentric cosmology — central eye, petal layers, triangulated subdivisions, and symbolic dots on the outer ring all read as diagrammatic geometry within 2 seconds. The palette (gold, rose, ultramarine, cream) is restrained and period-appropriate. Two things to sharpen: the counter-rotating bands and breathing petals are pleasant but generic — consider encoding specific Klint motifs like the dual spiral (evolution/involution) or her characteristic bisected color fields where one half is gold and the other blue, which would make the reference unmistakable. The 60k particles fill the frame well but the outermost triangles and dot clusters blur into a ring at default camera distance — tighten the outer geometry or bump point size so the triangulated subdivisions remain individually legible rather than dissolving into a halo.
